questions.prompt: shellcheck printed NOTHING for the broken script. The lesson?

options.b: silent failure is invisible to static analysis — strict mode at run time plus your own tracing are what catch it; the linter guards syntax, not honesty

questions.prompt: After your fix, someone runs it on a log with ZERO error lines. What happens?

options.b: grep exits 1 on no-match (L1.6), so under -e the script DIES: 'no errors' needs an explicit decision, e.g. grep … || true (L2.4), if empty-is-fine

questions.prompt: The trust rule this phase installs:

options.b: a script's exit code is only meaningful if every failure inside it either stops the script or is explicitly handled — otherwise 0 just means 'the last line ran'
